description: Engine data model: add SecretRefs map to ConnectionDef, multi-secret context helpers (WithSecrets/SecretsFrom), and update registry/pool resolution to resolve multiple secrets with backward-compatible fallback to legacy single SecretRef.
steps: 1. In /home/nuzirwan/project/rule-engine-api/.worktrees/multi-secret-refs/engine/internal/connect/connect.go: Add `SecretRefs map[string]string` field to `ConnectionDef` struct after `SecretRef string` (additive, backward compatible).

2. In /home/nuzirwan/project/rule-engine-api/.worktrees/multi-secret-refs/engine/internal/connect/connector.go: Add `secretsCtxKey struct{}` context key type, `WithSecrets(ctx context.Context, secrets map[string]Secret) context.Context` helper, and `SecretsFrom(ctx context.Context) (map[string]Secret, bool)` helper following the existing WithSecret/SecretFrom pattern.

3. In /home/nuzirwan/project/rule-engine-api/.worktrees/multi-secret-refs/engine/internal/connect/registry.go: Update `open()` method to resolve multiple secrets from `def.SecretRefs` when non-empty, falling back to legacy `def.SecretRef` when SecretRefs is empty. Call `WithSecrets(ctx, secrets)` and also `WithSecret(ctx, secrets["password"])` for backward compat when password key exists.
4. In /home/nuzirwan/project/rule-engine-api/.worktrees/multi-secret-refs/engine/internal/connect/pool.go: Apply identical multi-secret resolution logic in `(*ConnectionPool).open()` method.

5. Add unit tests in /home/nuzirwan/project/rule-engine-api/.worktrees/multi-secret-refs/engine/internal/connect/connector_test.go (or registry_test.go): Test WithSecrets/SecretsFrom round-trip, test registry.open() resolves multiple secrets, test legacy SecretRef fallback.
acceptance_criteria: ConnectionDef struct has both SecretRef string and SecretRefs map[string]string fields
WithSecrets and SecretsFrom context helpers exist and work correctly (round-trip test passes)
A connection with SecretRefs: {"password": "env:X", "username": "env:Y"} resolves both secrets
A connection with only SecretRef: "env:X" (no SecretRefs) is treated as {"password": "env:X"}
A connection with both set prefers SecretRefs over SecretRef
